feature1.prompt: django.utils.http.parse_http_date two digit year check is incorrect. The current implementation uses a fixed logic where two‐digit years from 0 to 69 are interpreted as 2000-2069 and those from 70 to 99 as 1970-1999, rather than comparing the two-digit year with the current year to decide if it should be adjusted. According to RFC 7231, a two-digit year that appears to be more than 50 years in the future must be interpreted as representing the most recent past year with the same last two digits. The fix requires updating the logic so that the current year is used to determine the proper century for the two-digit year.
feature1.hint_texts: This part involves updating the core logic in the parse_http_date function. Implement changes to use the current UTC year to compute the current century and adjust the two-digit year accordingly. The logic should determine if the two-digit year, when compared to the current year's last two digits, appears more than 50 years in the future, in which case it should adjust the century appropriately. Review the branch where the year is less than 100 and modify it to calculate the correct year based on the current time.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/utils/http.py; Function: parse_http_date. Begin by locating the block starting around the branch that checks if the year is less than 100 (see diff context at @@ -176,10 +176,14 @@). Modify the code to obtain the current UTC year, compute the current century, and adjust the year value accordingly.

feature2.prompt: django.utils.http.parse_http_date two digit year check is incorrect. According to RFC 7231, a two-digit year that appears more than 50 years in the future must be adjusted to represent the most recent past year with the same last two digits. The solution must ensure that dates in RFC 850 format are interpreted correctly in all cases.
feature2.hint_texts: This part is focused on enhancing the test suite to validate the updated date parsing logic. Extend the tests to cover edge cases for two-digit years by introducing scenarios that simulate different current years and examining how dates in RFC 850 format are interpreted. Use mocking to simulate the current date, and add tests to confirm that years which previously failed (such as those where the two-digit year is near the boundary) now pass according to the new logic.
feature2.entrypoint: File: tests/utils_tests/test_http.py; Function: test_parsing_rfc850. Modify this test file to add enhanced test cases, including the one referred to as test_parsing_year_less_than_70. collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the parse_http_date function in django/utils/http.py and the test file tests/utils_tests/test_http.py. The updated logic in the core function and the enhanced tests both rely on the same module and date parsing API.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 should expose a revised implementation of parse_http_date that correctly adjusts two-digit years based on the current date, while feature2 adds test cases that validate this new behavior under various scenarios. Integration testing should confirm that the new tests pass when run against the updated logic, ensuring that the changes work harmoniously.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers responsible for feature1 and feature2 must coordinate on the expected behavior of the date parsing logic. Regular discussions should ensure that the enhanced tests in feature2 accurately verify the adjustments made in feature1, and that any edge cases identified during testing are addressed in the logic update.
